passages.note: Bill overview lists Griffin as Prime sponsor of HB2756, which the governor signed.
House Final Reading vote list shows Griffin voting Y on HB2756's passage, 39-16-5-0-0.

passages.provision_quote: Supports policies that establish new customer classes, rate designs and cost allocation formulas for extra high load factor customers that are reasonable and necessary to prevent cost shifts to residential customers from extra high load factor customers.
passages.note: Enacted text sets reporting and commission-authorized rate-design requirements for extra high load factor customers to prevent cost-shifting to residential ratepayers, but has no moratorium, no absolute bar on cost pass-through, no impact-assessment or community-benefit terms, and does not touch permitting speed.

rows.reasoning: Griffin was Prime sponsor of HB2756 (2026) and voted Y on its final passage (39-16-5-0-0, not near-unanimous). The enacted text requires interconnection reporting on new extra high load factor customers and directs the corporation commission toward rate designs 'reasonable and necessary to prevent cost shifts to residential customers from extra high load factor customers,' but it adopts no construction moratorium, no absolute bar on cost pass-through, no impact-assessment or community-benefit terms, and no permitting change, so it shows direction toward protecting residential ratepayers without separating rungs 2, 3, or 4.
